articles.title: GPT-6 Astra sees the matrix and reprograms other AI models directly through their weights
articles.summary: MIT researchers show that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can read and deliberately rewrite the weights of other AI models without traditional training. In one experiment, Astra boosted a Qwen model's math accuracy from 7.9 to 48.1 percent by changing just 0.016 percent of its weights. The approach could fundamentally simplify AI optimization but still hits clear limits. The article GPT-6 Astra sees the matrix and reprograms other AI models directly through their weights appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Maximilian Schreiner

articles.title: Trainspotting: Learning Object-Centric 3D Reconstruction from Found Photos
articles.summary: State-of-the-art feedforward reconstruction models perform poorly on in-the-wild object-centric photo collections. They are trained largely on single-session object captures whose images vary in viewpoint while the object and its environment remain nearly fixed. Public photo archives contain a different form of multi-view data. They hold found photos of the same object or design: photos taken independently by many people across years, environments, cameras, and sometimes physical units. In this work, we introduce Trainspotting, a dataset of 12,068 objects and 311,886 photos from Wikimedia Commons. We reconstruct each object to recover camera poses, multi-view stereo depth, and object masks. We categorize the objects into three regimes: objects fixed at one site, objects that move between sites, and designs shared by many physical units. articles.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
articles.summary: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. articles.title: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval [R]
articles.summary: Author here. A short summary, since the title is a claim. Setup: key-value retrieval, 512 to 32K tokens, five open models (0.5B to 3B, four families). At equal length and equal evidence position, we fill the context either with neutral text or with statements in the format of the evidence. On every trial we log the loss on the correct answer and the attention mass on the evidence (a*). Findings: Neutral filler is nearly free: 0.97 to 1.00 accuracy up to 32K on Qwen2.5-1.5B (median loss 0.004 nats at 32K). Competing statements at the same positions: accuracy 0.11 to 0.21 (median loss 4.76 nats at 32K). The damage concentrates on statements that give the queried key a rival value: one such statement multiplies the loss by 9 to 110. log(1/a*) explains 35 to 58% of the variance in loss across 126,473 trials; log length explains 2 to 8%. articles.title: Hydrogen-1.0: open-weight scientific model beats GPT-6 Astra on FSR with 72% lower estimated output cost [P]
articles.summary: Hey everyone— we’re the Deep Principle team behind Mira AI Scientist. We just released Hydrogen-1.0, an open-weight model post-trained from GLM-5.3 for chemistry, materials science, and life sciences. Here’s how it performed in our evaluations: FrontierScience Research: 38.3% pass rate vs. 33.3% for GPT-6 Astra at max thinking—a 5 percentage point lead. Estimated output-side cost on FSR: $0.25 per problem vs. $0.88 for Astra at max thinking—about 72% lowerunder our evaluation setup. GPQA Diamond: 92.9% accuracy, compared with Kimi K3’s 93.5%. On separate internal task sets, Hydrogen also scored higher than GPT-6 Astra at max thinking on scientific computing (+5.13 percentage points) and single-step forward reaction prediction (+4.76 points). It trailed Astra on NMR structure elucidation (−3.33 points). The write-up covers the evaluations and five workflow examples. articles.title: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition
articles.summary: We introduce CoLa3D, a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition that, given a single whole-scene latent from either a single image or an existing scene mesh as input, directly outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be assembled back into a coherent scene. CoLa3D introduces a novel paradigm for 3D scene decomposition within a shared whole-scene latent, unlike alternatives that perform per-object generation in canonical spaces and then glue the objects back together with fragile pose and scale estimation. The network is a lightweight, flexible, and scalable query-based transformer that accepts various types of queries, including 2D masks, 3D points, and learnable queries, and learns to decompose the scene into objects in a compact latent space.
